overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance data shows massive traction for hypothetical 'What If' scenarios combined with extreme space anomalies and planetary phenomena. Specifically, videos using the 'What If You Fell Into...' hook structure (e.g., Liquid Diamond Planet, Planet of Burning Ice, Nonillion Diamond Planet) are drastically outperforming standard fact formats in both views and engagement (likes-per-view). Meanwhile, older psychological, standard space facts, and older biology videos posted over two weeks ago are plateauing rapidly in daily velocity. Engagement is heavily skewed toward interactive, high-stakes hypothetical curiosity loops.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) generated exceptionally high view velocity and engagement compared to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If You Fell Into...' hooks featuring extreme, bizarre, or high-value astronomical locations.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme planetary environments like 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1026 views) retain strong viewership.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form pieces focusing on bizarre, counter-intuitive physical laws or extreme weather on newly discovered exoplanets.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) show stagnant or negligible view-per-day growth.
weak_patterns.action: Reduce reliance on standard psychology or brain-hack tips unless framed through a high-stakes narrative or mystery micro-story.

weak_patterns.evidence: Standard declarative titles without an immersive hook or narrative question (e.g., 'The Star Colder Than Ice', views: 82) underperform significantly compared to second-person conditional framing.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid flat declarative statements; always frame the viewer directly into the scenario using 'You'.
